audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicted its own explanations. win[0] said Skill while whys[0] said Graves wins the opening exchange; win[2] said Skill while whys[2] described Sett taking over; win[3] said Graves while whys[3] said 'a fed Sett still wins'; win[5] said Graves while whys[5] called it a knife-edge in his favour. The packet chart matches the explanations, not the sides.
audit.why: The written reasoning is correct on the kits: Graves' single-ability level 1 out-ranges Sett before Haymaker exists, and Levels 3-5 belong to Sett because Knuckle Down's max-health damage and Haymaker's true damage both bypass True Grit resists.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the packet: Graves / Skill / Sett / Sett / Skill / Sett / Graves, with phase whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as a Graves spike ('Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback'), and the first-item stage was given to Graves although Sett's HP timing lands there.
audit.why: The Show Stopper is 400 range on 120/100/80s and carries the target bodily; Graves' Quickdraw is a 425 dash on 16-12s. The R is a Sett spike, not a Graves one. Sunfire-line HP also directly increases what Haymaker banks.
audit.corrected: Level 6 why now prices the 400 range and states that no dash escapes once it lands; first item flipped to Sett.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors, one of them dangerous. (a) Facebreaker is called a 'pull-stun' everywhere — it only stuns when enemies are on OPPOSITE sides of Sett; a lone target is slowed instead. In a solo lane that is the normal case and it changes every step-up. (b) The page tells you to 'bait it, then E-dash out of the carry' on his R — you cannot dash out of The Show Stopper once it lands. Following that advice gets a player killed.
audit.why: Riot text, Sett E: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Sett R: 'Sett carries an enemy champion through the air and slams them into the ground' — the R also carries a grounding flag, which shuts dashes off.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker's one-sided behaviour written into early, whys[2], spikes[0], the cooldown block, dosFull[0] and report[5]; the R advice changed to dodging the 400-range cast rather than escaping the carry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Knuckle Down appears nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Sett Q, 9/8/7/6/5s, free to cast: 'Sett's next two attacks deal additional damage based off of the target's max health. Sett also gains Move Speed while moving towards enemy champions.' Max-health damage ignores your True Grit stacking, and the move speed is why a Graves who starts walking away still gets caught.
audit.corrected: Added to early and to phases[3].why.

audit.why: Packet flagged 'Smoke Screen's' as a wrong name — false positive; it is Graves' real W. The page's use of 'nearsight' for the smoke is also accurate to Riot's text ('creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range'). The one place W was wrongly called a blind is report[10], which is fixed.
audit.corrected: report[10] blind wording corrected; the rest left alone.

edits.after: Knuckle Down's max-health hits and Haymaker's true damage ignore your True Grit — don't brawl him flat-footed here.

edits.before: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. It governs your forward steps. - E dash spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — 490 range, 10-16s, and it stuns only if enemies stand on both sides of him; alone you are merely slowed. It governs your forward steps. - E dash spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Facebreaker stuns only with enemies on both sides — never stand opposite a minion. Commit on its 10-16s cooldown.

edits.before: Track Sett’s Facebreaker: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Sett’s Facebreaker: 490 range, and it stuns only when enemies stand on both sides of him — solo you are slowed instead. Its cooldown is the green light.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W cuts sight range on tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip.

edits.before: Sett's E pull-stun comes online and his W is loaded, letting him lock you in melee and out-grit your shells before your own kit is fully stocked.
edits.after: Facebreaker comes online and Haymaker is loaded — but it stuns only with enemies on both sides, so solo you eat a slow and his max-health Q punches.

edits.before: His R suppress-slam can flip any even trade into a kill, but your E escape and Smoke Screen vision-cut can answer it — whoever lands their cooldown first takes the window.
edits.after: The Show Stopper flips any even trade into a kill and once he has you no dash escapes it — answer it before the 400-range cast, not after, with spacing and smoke.

edits.before: His Bami's/Sunfire grit timing matches your first-item duel spike, so the all-in stays a knife-edge until your Eclipse burst fully outscales his store.
edits.after: His Bami's/Sunfire HP timing beats your first-item duel spike — every shell you land banks into a bigger Haymaker, so this window belongs to him.

edits.before: Sett's W banks the damage he takes into a true-damage Haymaker, and his E (Facebreaker) pull-stun comes online around 3 — this is his window, so don't trade point-blank shells into his grit before your second E charge is stocked.
edits.after: Sett's W banks the damage he takes into a true-damage Haymaker, and Facebreaker (E, 490 range, 10-16s) arrives around 3 — but it stuns only with enemies on both sides of him, so solo you take a slow. Don't feed Grit before both E charges are stocked.

edits.before: His R (The Show Stopper) suppress-slams you out of any even trade for a kill; bait it, then E-dash out of the carry, and only commit your own R once his suppress is on cooldown.
edits.after: The Show Stopper is 400 range on 80-120s and carries you bodily — no dash gets you out once it lands, so stay outside that radius and commit your own R only after his is spent.

edits.before: Sett owns the very first all-in the moment his W is up — Haymaker banks the damage he takes into a true-damage smash, so unloading point-blank shells into his face just loads his gun, and his passive alternating punches out-auto you in a stand-still brawl. Don't sit on top of him before both E charges are stocked; last-hit at the edge of your Q cone and only step in when his W is empty or on cooldown. The one thing you must never eat is a raw E pull-stun into his combo — hold an E charge to dash out of the Facebreaker rather than burning both to chase.
edits.after: Sett owns the very first all-in the moment his W is up — Haymaker banks the damage he takes into a true-damage smash, so unloading point-blank shells into his face just loads his gun, and Knuckle Down adds max-health damage to his next two punches plus move speed toward you. Don't sit on top of him before both E charges are stocked; last-hit at the edge of your Q cone and step in only when his W is empty or on cooldown. Facebreaker stuns only when enemies stand on both sides of him — keep no minion opposite you and it lands as a slow.

edits.before: This is the grind. Through 4-5 your True Grit armor and E charges compound, but a fed Sett still wins the stand-still smash war, and at 6 his R suppress-slam turns any even trade into a kill — respect it, bait it, then E-dash out of the carry. Your real turn is the first-item spike: with Eclipse or Essence Reaver you E-kite his slow W windup, drop Smoke Screen so the nearsight blanks his vision and he whiffs the Haymaker, then burst Q+auto+R from a full magazine. Until then, trade in short bursts and reset — never get caught reloading inside his E range.
edits.after: This is the grind. Through 4-5 your True Grit armor and E charges compound, but Knuckle Down's max-health punches and Haymaker's true damage both go straight through resists, and at 6 The Show Stopper turns any even trade into a kill — it is only 400 range, so dash out of the cast, because nothing gets you out of the carry. Your real turn is the first-item spike: with Eclipse or Essence Reaver you E-kite his slow W windup, drop Smoke Screen so the sight cut makes him whiff the Haymaker, then burst Q+auto+R from a full magazine. Never get caught reloading inside his 490 E range.

notes: The most important fix here is safety-critical: the page told the reader to E-dash out of The Show Stopper's carry, which is impossible — Sett's R carries the target and also grounds, so the dash has to happen before the 400-range cast. Second: Facebreaker was called a pull-stun throughout, but Riot's own text says a target alone on one side is slowed, not stunned, which is the normal case in a solo lane. Knuckle Down was missing from the page entirely despite being his max-health damage and his only gap-closing tool. UNVERIFIED, left alone: 'his R slam scales on that HP' in late and wants.foe[2] — Riot's text does not state a bonus-health ratio on The Show Stopper, so I did not touch or repeat the claim.
